title: Management-plane entry: unauthenticated -> admin plane takeover
binary: /tmp/cw-audit/bin/cheesewaf — CheeseWAF 0.4.5-beta (dev-local, unknown), built from the clean worktree /tmp/cw-audit/src at 3216e72d

instances.harness_note: harness/env.sh port map for T1 changed during the run (18081/19441/19091 -> 28081/29441/29091); the instance was rebuilt and every captured request in this report uses admin=29441. Config and instance.env snapshots are in artifacts/T1/_instance/.
instances.artifacts: security-validation/attack-chain/artifacts/T1 (per case: cmd.txt, trace.txt with raw wire bytes, headers.txt, body.txt, meta.txt)

findings.title: [REFUTED] CSRF double-submit skip via bogus Authorization header was a harness artifact (secret placeholder resolved to a valid token)
findings.asset: cheesewaf admin API (127.0.0.1:29441) — internal/api/middleware/csrf.go + session-authenticated route group /api/auth/* (internal/api/router.go:240-249)
findings.preconditions: Attacker can make a request to the admin listener that carries both (a) the victim's cookie session and (b) an attacker-chosen Authorization header. Browsers block custom headers on cross-origin no-cors requests, so this needs a header-injection position (malicious extension, local process driving the browser, header-rewriting proxy) or any same-origin script foothold. Entry cookie + valid admin credentials are required for the victim session.
chain: T1-14: unauthenticated client mints the entry cookie at /g7k2m9 (302 + cheesewaf_admin_entry).
T1-15/01: POST /api/auth/login issues cheesewaf_session (HttpOnly) + cheesewaf_csrf.
T1-15/04: POST /api/auth/logout with the cookie session and no X-CSRF-Token is correctly rejected (403 CSRF_INVALID) — the intended control.
T1-15/18: the same call with the extra header `Authorization: Bearer cwapi_<anything>` is accepted (200) and executed: /api/auth/refresh returns a fresh csrf token and user object.
T1-15/21: same trick on /api/auth/logout returns {"revoked":true} and the session is dead (T1-15/22 -> 401).

Root cause: CSRFMiddleware decides the exemption from the raw Authorization header (`strings.HasPrefix(bearerToken(r), "cwapi_")`) but the request was in fact authenticated by the cookie — tokens.Middleware/SessionMiddleware use SessionToken(r), which prefers the cookie, so the bogus bearer is never validated.

evidence.request: POST /api/auth/refresh with Cookie session and no X-CSRF-Token -> 403; with literal "Authorization: Bearer cwapi_forged" -> 401 (reproduced manually).
evidence.response: Control reproduced: 403 without header, 401 with a literal forged cwapi_ value.
evidence.control: Original 200 trace used the secret placeholder $$...$$, not a literal token.

findings.impact: Not exploitable: managementAuth rejects any invalid cwapi_ bearer with 401 before CSRF runs; the 200 observed in the original run came from a harness secret placeholder that resolved to a real token. Literal cwapi_ attacks return 401.
findings.repro:
1) mint entry cookie: curl --noproxy '*' -A 'audit-ua' -c jar -b jar http://127.0.0.1:29441/g7k2m9
2) login: curl ... -b jar -c jar -X POST .../api/auth/login -d '{"username":"admin","password":"<pw>"}'
3) control: curl -b jar -c jar -X POST .../api/auth/logout  -> 403 CSRF_INVALID
4) bypass: same call + -H 'Authorization: Bearer cwapi_anything' -> 200 {"data":{"revoked":true}}; a follow-up GET /api/system returns 401.

findings.title: First-install static-asset allowlist trusts the raw request path while the file resolver normalizes it — console SPA is served without the entry cookie (`/assets/../index.html` -> 200 vs `/index.html` -> 418)
findings.asset: console.login.security_entry gate during first install — internal/cli/service.go allowAdminEntranceAt (isAdminStaticAssetPath on r.URL.Path) vs serveAdminStaticFile (path.Clean)
findings.preconditions: security_entry.enabled=true and first install still pending (setup.NeedsSetup == true). Reachability of the admin listener.
chain: The gate short-circuits for `setup.NeedsSetup(cfg.Setup.DataDir) && (GET|HEAD) && isAdminStaticAssetPath(r.URL.Path)`.
isAdminStaticAssetPath only checks a raw string prefix (`/assets/`), while the static resolver uses `path.Clean` on the same path.
GET /assets/../index.html (sent literally over a raw socket, no client normalisation) is therefore allowed by the gate and then resolves to `index.html` inside the web root.
Direct /index.html and / are still 418.

evidence.request:
GET /assets/../index.html HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:29441
User-Agent: audit-ua
(no cookie; sent over a raw socket so the path is not normalised by the client)

variants: /assets/./../index.html, /assets//../index.html, /assets/%2e%2e/index.html
evidence.response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 (false) …
… (1507 bytes, the console SPA shell)
evidence.control:
GET /index.html without cookie -> 418 teapot (T1-12/09); GET / without cookie -> 418 (T1-12/07).
Escapes out of the web root are refused: /assets/..%2f..%2fdata%2fsetup.token -> 404 and /assets/..%2f..%2f..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd -> 404 (T1-12/raw/15,16), i.e. no arbitrary file read.
After setup completes the allowlist is gone: /assets/%2e%2e/index.html -> 418 (T1-13/09).

findings.impact: Before the console is configured, an unauthenticated client can retrieve the console static shell (and any other file under web/dist reachable that way) without the entry cookie, defeating the intended 418 camouflage for that class of paths. Nothing outside the web root is readable and /api/* stays closed, so the practical loss is the entry-gate concealment itself.
findings.repro:
printf 'GET /assets/../index.html HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:29441
Connection: close

' | nc 127.0.0.1 29441  -> 200 + SPA shell, while GET /index.html -> 418.

findings.title: Entry-path strength (8-64 alphanumeric) is enforced only by the setup API; config validation accepts arbitrary short/guessable segments that the 418 gate then honours
findings.asset: internal/setup/security_entry.go ValidateSecurityEntrySegment (8-64, [A-Za-z0-9]) vs internal/config/validator.go validateSecurityEntry (absolute clean path only)
findings.preconditions: Operator configures console.login.security_entry.path by editing YAML/API config instead of finishing the wizard (the harness does exactly this).
chain: POST /api/setup with security_entry_path=g7k2m9 is rejected: 400 SETUP_VALIDATION 'admin security entry must contain 8-64 ASCII letters or digits'.
The identical segment is accepted from config, and instance.sh set T1 ENTRY_ENABLED=true starts the gate on /g7k2m9.
The gate happily mints the entry cookie for that 6-character path (302 + Set-Cookie).

evidence.response:
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":{"code":"SETUP_VALIDATION","message":"setup validation failed: admin security entry must contain 8-64 ASCII letters or digits"…}}
evidence.control:
Control A — same request with security_entry_path=g7k2m9audit: HTTP/1.1 200 {"data":{"security_entry_path":"/g7k2m9audit","setup_complete":true…}} (T1-13/04).
Control B — the 6-char path taken from YAML is live: GET /g7k2m9 -> 302 + Set-Cookie cheesewaf_admin_entry (T1-14/04).
Control C — structural checks still apply from YAML: paths containing '..' are rejected by config validation (validator.go:2536).

findings.impact: The entry path is the only thing hiding the console from a scanner; a short/low-entropy segment (e.g. /g7k2m9, /admin1) is brute-forceable, after which the login endpoint becomes reachable unauthenticated (subject to rate limiting). Also makes the harness default (and any wizard-less deployment) weaker than the wizard's own policy.
findings.repro: Set console.login.security_entry.path: "/a" in YAML, start serve with entry enabled, GET /a -> 302 + entry cookie; POST /api/setup with the same value -> 400.

findings.title: `/healthz` on the admin listener is served outside the security-entry gate (unauthenticated), while /health is allowlisted and /readyz is 418
findings.asset: internal/cli/service.go withAdapterHealth (mounted before adminHandler) + internal/adapterapi/handler.go health (no authorization)
findings.preconditions: security_entry.enabled=true (any post-setup state). Reachability of the admin listener.
chain: withAdapterHealth routes r.URL.Path == "/healthz" straight to the adapter API handler, before the admin entrance gate runs.
adapterapi health() performs no token/loopback check and returns {"status":"ok"}.
The gate's own allowlist does not mention /healthz (only /health, /health/*, public metrics), so the two paths behave inconsistently.

evidence.request:
GET /healthz HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:29441
User-Agent: audit-ua
Accept: application/json
(no cookies)
evidence.control:
GET /readyz (unknown path, same client) -> 418 teapot (T1-17/13) and GET /healthz equivalent on an unknown /healthz subpath is gated.
GET / without cookie -> 418 (T1-14/01); GET /api/v1/adapter/inspect without cookie -> 403 admin entry required (T1-17/11) — so only /healthz escapes the gate.

findings.impact: Confirms the admin listener is alive to any scanner regardless of the entry gate; combined with the version banner in /api/auth/login-options it supports fingerprinting. No administrative data is returned.
findings.repro: curl --noproxy '*' http://127.0.0.1:29441/healthz -> 200 {"status":"ok"} with no cookie; curl .../readyz -> 418.

findings.title: Login lockout and captcha enforcement are keyed on the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For when the peer is loopback, so header rotation defeats the 5-failure lockout
findings.preconditions: Admin console not public (server.admin_public=false) and the socket peer is loopback (documented single-host reverse-proxy deployment). The proxy must forward client-supplied XFF unfiltered.
chain: trustedLoginClientIP() accepts the right-most X-Forwarded-For entry from a loopback peer, and loginRateLimitKeys() builds 'client:<ip>' from it.
Five wrong passwords from 203.0.113.9 lock that key: 6th attempt and even the CORRECT password return 429 LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED for 5 minutes.
The same correct password from 203.0.113.10 (one header value change) returns 200, so the lockout is per header value, not per real client.
The same header also disables the loopback captcha skip: without XFF the login succeeds with captcha enabled, with XFF the identical request is rejected 401 INVALID_CAPTCHA.

evidence.request:
POST /api/auth/login HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9
{"username":"admin","password":"wrong-password"}   (x5, then the correct password)
evidence.control:
Correct password from X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.10 -> 200 (lock is per source key) [T1-16/03]; from 203.0.113.14 after locking .9 -> 200 [T1-16/06].
Captcha control: with CAPTCHA_ENABLED=true, loopback login without XFF -> 200 [T1-18/04]; identical request with X-Forwarded-For -> 401 INVALID_CAPTCHA [T1-18/05].

findings.impact: In the common 'nginx/traefik on the same host' deployment the password-spray ceiling (5 tries / 5 min / client) can be reset at will by rotating the X-Forwarded-For value, and the per-source captcha challenge can be avoided the same way. Conversely an attacker can pin a victim IP (or omit XFF inside the console) to force 5-minute lockouts — a trivial login DoS for one source.
findings.repro: for i in 1..5: curl -X POST .../api/auth/login -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9' -d '{bad}'; then the same with the correct password -> 429; repeat with -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.10' -> 200.

findings.title: Login lockout gives 5 attempts per source with no Retry-After and no challenge fallback — cheap account/source denial of service
findings.preconditions: Any client able to reach the login endpoint through the entry gate.
chain: 5 failed password attempts (or even 5 attempts with a syntactically valid but non-existent account) lock the source and the account-source key for 5 minutes.
The 429 response carries no Retry-After and the correct password is refused for the whole lock window.

evidence.request: POST /api/auth/login with wrong password x5 from X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9
evidence.response:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":{"code":"LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED","message":"too many failed login attempts"…}}
(headers: no Retry-After)
evidence.control:
Same 5 failures for a non-existent account return the uniform 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS in ~66 ms, identical to the existing-account timing (T1-16/04), so enumeration is not possible but locking does not require a real account.
Login endpoint is unreachable without the entry cookie (T1-15/12 -> 403 admin entry required), which limits the attacker pool to someone who already found the entry path.

findings.impact: A single source can be locked out of the console for 5 minutes with 5 requests; without Retry-After, clients cannot back off gracefully. Low severity because the lock is time-bounded and the endpoint sits behind the entry gate.
findings.repro: 5x wrong password then the correct one -> 429 for 5 minutes; headers contain no Retry-After.

coverage.scope: T1 management-plane entry track: setup-token gate, first-install surface, setup completion, 418 security entry gate (path normalisation, static assets, cookie minting/binding), session + CSRF, login throttling/enumeration, health surface, captcha and admin-TLS variants.

cases.T1-10: setup token gate — /api/setup, /api/setup/probe, /api/setup/integrations/postgres/test, /api/setup/draft all 401 SETUP_TOKEN_REQUIRED without the header; /api/setup/status stays public (needs_setup=true); control: valid token -> 200 with setup session cookie.
cases.T1-11: token shape/oracle matrix — wrong token (401 'invalid'), 40-char prefix (401), uppercase (401), token in query (401 'required'), token in Authorization (401), empty header (401), duplicated header (401, first value wins); HTTP header trailing whitespace is stripped by net/http so 'token + space' is accepted (200) — transport behaviour, not a bypass; valid token without setup session -> 401 SETUP_SESSION_REQUIRED.
cases.T1-12: first-install surface — probe issues cheesewaf_setup_session (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, 30 min); draft get/patch require that session; Origin: https://evil.example -> 403 SETUP_ORIGIN_DENIED while Origin http://localhost:9999 and no-Origin -> 200 (isLocalOrSameOrigin treats any localhost origin as local); postgres test is token-gated and returns 502 SETUP_POSTGRES_UNREACHABLE without echoing the password; static-asset allowlist path-normalisation (see T1-F2) with 404s for web-root escapes.
cases.T1-13: setup completion — security_entry_path validation (too short 400, traversal 400), weak password 400, correct token -> 200 + admin user + entry path persisted, immediate replay -> 409 SETUP_ALREADY_COMPLETE, wrong token after completion -> 409 (state is checked before the token, so no post-setup token oracle), setup.token/setup.url deleted, /setup SPA still served.
cases.T1-14: 418 entry gate — / and /api/* without the entry cookie (418 HTML vs 403 JSON), entry mint 302 + HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax cookie, console 200 with cookie, API 401 (auth) with entry cookie only, POST/PUT/OPTIONS on the entry path 418 (only GET/HEAD mint), HEAD mints, trailing slash / double slash / dot-segment / percent-encoded entry path all mint (filepath.Clean + URL decoding), uppercase does not, returnTo passthrough, cookie tampering (wrong UA, expiry edit, truncated MAC, malformed) all 418, GET /api%2fsystem -> 403 JSON while //api/system -> 418 (triage quirk, no bypass), raw traversal past the entry path to /api/system -> 418 and no cookie.
cases.T1-15: session + CSRF — login issues HttpOnly session + readable CSRF (SameSite=Strict), authenticated reads work, logout/refresh rejected 403 CSRF_INVALID without the header, accepted with the matching header or the urlencoded csrf_token form field, forged/empty/duplicate CSRF rejected, fixed session value not adopted (no fixation), login impossible without the entry cookie (403), wrong password 401 uniform, entry cookie is UA-bound even with a valid session (403). See T1-F1 for the cwapi_ bearer CSRF skip.
cases.T1-16: login throttling/enumeration — 5 failures then 429 LOGIN_RATE_LIMITED (also for the correct password), lock scoped to the XFF-derived source key (fresh source -> 200), non-existent account returns the same 401/timing as a wrong password (~66 ms), syntactically invalid username returns 400 USERNAME_INVALID in ~1 ms (format only), 429 has no Retry-After.
cases.T1-17: health/metrics — /health, /health/live, /health/ready, /health/cluster reachable without the entry cookie (documented allowlist), /metrics and /api/metrics 403 without it, /metrics 404 when Prometheus is disabled, /api/metrics 200 with session, /healthz 200 outside the gate (T1-F4), /readyz 418.
cases.T1-18: captcha variant (CAPTCHA_ENABLED=true) — login-options advertises captcha mode=slider and the product version, challenge issuance returns a 320x150 slider PNG, loopback login skips captcha (200), any X-Forwarded-For disables that skip (401 INVALID_CAPTCHA even with the right password), forged receipt/proof rejected 401, issuance throttled per client (15x200 then 503 CAPTCHA_CAPACITY_REACHED).
cases.T1-19: admin TLS variant (ADMIN_TLS_ENABLED=true) — HTTP/2 over TLS1.3 with a self-signed CheeseWAF Admin leaf (C=…, SAN 127.0.0.1/localhost), plain HTTP to the TLS port -> 400 'Client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server.', HSTS present on gate responses, entry cookie gains Secure, session cookies switch to the __Host- prefix, login + API work over TLS, an entry cookie minted over plain HTTP is still accepted over HTTPS (no scheme binding) while the UA binding holds (418).

controls: no set-up token vs valid set-up token (T1-10/01..05 vs 06)
wrong token vs correct token for probe/draft (T1-11/01 vs 06/08)
entry cookie absent vs present (T1-14/01,02 vs 04,05)
entry cookie only vs cookie + session (T1-14/06 vs T1-15/02)
CSRF header absent vs present, and cwapi_-prefixed vs arbitrary bearer (T1-15/04,06,07,17,18,19)
locked source vs fresh source (T1-16/02 vs 03/06)
loopback login with and without X-Forwarded-For under captcha (T1-18/04 vs 05)
plain HTTP vs TLS on the same admin port (T1-19/01 vs 02)
first-install static allowlist before vs after setup completion (T1-12/10 vs T1-13/09)
refuted: Setup-token bypass through query parameter, Authorization header, uppercase, prefix, empty value or duplicated header — all 401 (T1-11).
Setup-token replay after completion (expecting a token oracle) — 409 SETUP_ALREADY_COMPLETE, token file deleted (T1-13/05,06).
Entry-cookie forgery / replay with another User-Agent, edited expiry, truncated MAC or malformed value — all 418 (T1-14/12..16).
Reaching /api/* by traversal or encoding through the entry gate — 418 HTML or 403 JSON, never a minted cookie plus API body (T1-14/raw/20..23).
Arbitrary file read through the static allowlist — traversal beyond web/dist returns 404 (T1-12/raw/15,16).
Privilege escalation by pairing a bogus cwapi_ bearer with a cookie session — management-auth routes answer 401 (T1-15/20); only CSRF is skipped.
Session fixation via a pre-set session cookie — login issues a fresh session and the planted value never authenticates (T1-15/23,24).
CSRF bypass with a duplicate/mismatched-length token or the urlencoded form field without the cookie value — 403 (T1-15/25).
gaps: Setup-token file permission/TTL handling and the setup.url receipt were observed (0600, token deleted on completion) but not attacked beyond the gate ordering.
Passkey/TOTP login paths, /api/auth/session/bootstrap semantics and the entry gate's behaviour under admin_public=true (XFF ignored) were out of scope for T1.
Concurrent-login caps (32) and the full audit-log correlation were not exercised.

notes: T1-F1 refuted after manual replay: the harness secret placeholder resolved to a valid management token; literal forged cwapi_ values return 401 before CSRF.
